title: The Art of Chivalry: European Arms and Armor from The Metropolitan Museum of Art
authors: Helmut Nickel, Stuart W. Pyhrr and Leonid Tarassuk
note: Museum exhibition catalogue covering European arms and their artistic and courtly contexts. Free PDF on the publication page.

title: Islamic Arms and Armor in The Metropolitan Museum of Art
authors: David G. Alexander, with contributions by Stuart W. Pyhrr and Will Kwiatkowski
note: Detailed catalogue of 126 objects, including swords, yatagans, inscriptions and decorative techniques. Free PDF on the publication page.

title: The Academy of the Sword: Illustrated Fencing Books 1500–1800
note: Catalogue of illustrated fencing books and associated weapons. Useful for understanding period images as sources. Free PDF on the publication page.

title: Art of the Samurai: Japanese Arms and Armor, 1156–1868
note: Museum catalogue of Japanese blades, fittings, armor and related arts. Free PDF on the publication page.

title: Sword and Dagger Pommels Associated with the Crusades, Part I
note: Metropolitan Museum Journal 46, pp. 133–144. The opening discussion on p. 133 explains European hilt assembly and later remounting.

title: The Japanese Blade: Technology and Manufacture
note: Museum essay explaining forging, hardening and the separate crafts involved in sword mountings.

title: Techniques of Decoration on Arms and Armor
note: Museum essay distinguishing techniques such as engraving, etching and inlay; surface appearance alone is not a material analysis.

title: Wood and Woodworking in Anglo-Scandinavian and Medieval York
note: York Archaeological Trust monograph, The Archaeology of York 17/13. Includes archaeological discussion of woodworking axes and their forms.
